## Purpose and Delivery Surfaces
Mem0 is a memory layer for AI agents: it extracts durable facts from interactions, retrieves relevant memories, and supports user/session/agent scoping. This repository ships several independently usable surfaces:
- Python SDK: `mem0/__init__.py`, `mem0/memory/main.py`
- TypeScript SDK, including managed-platform client and OSS implementation: `mem0-ts/src/client/mem0.ts`, `mem0-ts/src/oss/src/memory/index.ts`
- Node and Python CLIs: `cli/node/src/index.ts`, `cli/python/src/mem0_cli/__main__.py`
- Self-hosted administration/auth service and dashboard: `server/main.py`, `server/dashboard/src/app/(root)/dashboard/layout.tsx`
- Agent-framework/editor plugins and packaged skills under `integrations/` and `skills/`.

## Core Memory Pipeline
The Python OSS `Memory` implementation is the principal memory orchestration boundary. It accepts messages/text plus identity filters, uses configured providers to extract memory candidates, then persists and retrieves them.
- Orchestrator and lifecycle: `mem0/memory/main.py`, `mem0/memory/setup.py`
- Shared contracts/storage coordination: `mem0/memory/base.py`, `mem0/memory/storage.py`
- Prompt definitions and memory-specific processing: `mem0/configs/prompts.py`, `mem0/memory/utils.py`

Primary flow is: caller supplies conversation → LLM-based extraction produces facts → embeddings/vector persistence index facts → later query is embedded and searched under scope filters → optional keyword/entity signals and reranking refine results. The application/agent, not Mem0, incorporates returned memories into its generation prompt.

## Provider and Storage Abstractions
Provider implementations are intentionally separated from memory orchestration through base interfaces and factory/configuration layers. This makes LLMs, embedders, rerankers, and vector databases replaceable infrastructure dependencies.
- LLM adapters/interfaces: `mem0/llms/base.py`, `mem0/llms/openai.py`, `mem0/llms/anthropic.py`
- Embedding adapters/interfaces: `mem0/embeddings/base.py`, `mem0/embeddings/openai.py`
- Vector-store interfaces/adapters: `mem0/vector_stores/base.py`, `mem0/vector_stores/qdrant.py`, `mem0/vector_stores/pgvector.py`
- Construction/configuration boundary: `mem0/utils/factory.py`, `mem0/configs/base.py`

Supported external services include OpenAI by default, other hosted/local LLM and embedding providers, and stores such as Qdrant, pgvector, Pinecone, Redis, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, and cloud vector services. Rerankers are a distinct post-retrieval stage: `mem0/reranker/base.py`, `mem0/reranker/llm_reranker.py`.

## Retrieval Enrichment and Local State
Retrieval can combine semantic similarity with BM25 keyword matching, entity extraction/linking, scoring, and temporal/expiration behavior. These are algorithmic concerns below the public `Memory` API, not caller responsibilities.
- Entity and scoring logic: `mem0/utils/entity_extraction.py`, `mem0/utils/scoring.py`
- Notices and memory behavior: `mem0/memory/notices.py`, `mem0/memory/oss_notices_config.json`
- TypeScript OSS equivalents: `mem0-ts/src/oss/src/utils/entity_extraction.ts`, `mem0-ts/src/oss/src/utils/bm25.ts`
- Local history options include SQLite and Supabase: `mem0-ts/src/oss/src/storage/SQLiteManager.ts`, `mem0-ts/src/oss/src/storage/SupabaseHistoryManager.ts`.

## Managed Platform Clients, CLI, and Telemetry
The platform client is an HTTP API boundary for managed Mem0 capabilities (memory CRUD/search, entities, projects, organizations, exports, webhooks, events). It is separate from the OSS in-process engine.
- Python client: `mem0/client/main.py`, `mem0/client/project.py`
- TypeScript client: `mem0-ts/src/client/mem0.ts`, `mem0-ts/src/client/config.ts`
- CLI command routing/backends: `cli/node/src/commands/memory.ts`, `cli/node/src/backend/platform.ts`, `cli/python/src/mem0_cli/commands/memory.py`
- Telemetry is implemented per surface: `mem0/memory/telemetry.py`, `cli/node/src/telemetry.ts`.

CLIs detect/configure execution context, retain local state, then route commands to platform backends or configured workflows rather than duplicating the memory algorithm.

## Self-Hosted and Integration Boundaries
The self-hosted stack is containerized and pairs a Python service with a Next.js dashboard. It provides auth, API keys, entities, and request-management surfaces; database schema evolution is Alembic-managed.
- Service entry/auth/database: `server/main.py`, `server/auth.py`, `server/db.py`
- HTTP routers: `server/routers/auth.py`, `server/routers/api_keys.py`, `server/routers/entities.py`
- Deployment: `server/docker-compose.yaml`, `server/Dockerfile`
- Dashboard API client/auth boundary: `server/dashboard/src/utils/api.ts`, `server/dashboard/src/hooks/use-auth.ts`

Agent plugins package a common memory protocol—MCP server, command interface, hooks, scoped capture, async flush, and skills—adapted to host-specific plugin manifests. The shared build/runtime source is `integrations/agent-plugin-core/python/memory_core.py`, `integrations/agent-plugin-core/python/mcp_server.py`, and `integrations/agent-plugin-core/build/build.py`; concrete adapters include `integrations/claude-code-plugin/adapters/claude/hook.py` and `integrations/codex-plugin/hooks/adapter.py`.
